open.text: In January nineteen sixty-four, the U.S. Navy intercepted a secret Soviet radar, by listening to the Moon.
open.heard: In January 1964, the U .S. Navy intercepted a secret Soviet radar by listening to the moon.

u2.text: A U two had photographed its giant antenna at Sari Shagan, a Soviet missile range.
u2.heard: U -2 had photographed its giant antenna at Sarishagon, a Soviet missile range.

horizon.text: But radar waves travel in straight lines. From deep inside the U.S.S.R., they skim past the horizon into space.
horizon.heard: But radar waves travel in straight lines. From deep inside the U .S .S .R., they skim past the horizon into space.

nuke.text: In nineteen sixty-two, it was heard briefly, off the ionized cloud of a Soviet nuclear test. They needed a steadier mirror.
nuke.heard: In 1962, it was heard briefly off the ionized cloud of a Soviet nuclear test. They needed a steadier mirror.

geometry.text: When it sat low on the radar's horizon, and above America too, a sliver of each pulse bounced back down.
geometry.heard: When it sat low on the radar's horizon, and above America, too, a sliver of each pulse bounced back down.

faint.text: The echo was over a million billion times weaker than ten miles from the radar. Only hundred-and-fifty-foot dishes could hear it.
faint.heard: The Echo was over a million billion times weaker than 10 miles from the radar. Only 150 -foot dishes could hear it.

sites.text: The Navy's dish on Chesapeake Bay got it first; the CIA's, at Stanford, in nineteen sixty-five. Geometry allowed about eighteen hours a month.
sites.heard: The Navy's dish on Chesapeake Bay got it first, the CIA's, at Stanford, in 1965. Geometry allowed about 18 hours a month.

found.text: It was enough: computer-controlled scanning, a spread-spectrum mode, about twenty-five megawatts of peak power. A new anti-missile radar.
found.heard: It was enough, computer -controlled scanning, a spread spectrum mode, about 25 megawatts of peak power, a new anti -missile radar.

practice.text: Soviet operators even locked it onto the Moon, for practice.
practice.heard: Soviet operators even locked it onto the moon for practice.

exhibit.text: Years earlier, a touring Soviet exhibition showed off a Loonik: the final stage of a Moon rocket. Surely, a mock-up.
exhibit.heard: Years earlier, a touring Soviet exhibition showed off a lunatic, the final stage of a moon rocket, surely a mock -up.

real.text: It wasn't. U.S. intelligence officers spent a day with it: a real production vehicle, engine removed.
real.heard: It wasn't U .S. Intelligence officers spent a day with it, a real production vehicle engine removed.

icbm.text: That data helped the CIA measure the Soviet I.C.B.M.: eighteen thousand pounds thrown thirty-eight hundred miles.
icbm.heard: That data helped the CIA measure the Soviet I. C .B .M. 18 ,000 pounds thrown 3 ,800 miles.

borrow.text: Later, for its factory markings, the CIA borrowed it. Overnight.
borrow.heard: Later, for its factory markings, the CIA borrowed it overnight.

truck.text: It left as the day's last truck. At the final turnoff, a new driver took the wheel. The real one spent the night in a hotel.
truck.heard: It left as the day's last truck. At the final turnoff, a new driver took the wheel. The real one spent the night in a hotel.

yard.text: In a rented salvage yard, four specialists opened the roof, unbolted the base, and slipped inside, shoes off.
yard.heard: In a rented salvage yard, four specialists opened the roof, unbolted the base, and slipped inside. Shoes off.

dawn.text: By seven A.M., the truck was at the rail yard. The Soviet checker showed no surprise.
dawn.heard: By 7 a .m., the truck was at the rail yard. The Soviet checker showed no surprise.

results.text: The markings revealed the likely manufacturer, and that it was the fifth one built.
results.heard: The markings revealed the likely manufacturer, and that it was the fifth one built.

nosign.text: The CIA saw no sign the Soviets ever knew.
nosign.heard: The CIA saw no sign the Soviets ever knew.

end.text: Both files stayed classified until the nineteen-nineties.
end.heard: Both files stayed classified until the 1990s.
